## Step 1 — read the canonical recipe first

Run this and read the whole file before you change any code:

```bash
curl -sSL -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' https://react.doctor/docs/rules/react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup.md -o /tmp/rd-cleanup.md && cat /tmp/rd-cleanup.md
```

Read the validation prompt and the fix prompt in full. The recipe names two false-positive predicates. Apply them honestly. Do not delete a timer to silence the rule. Do not add an empty `return () => {}`. Do not add a lint suppression comment.

## Step 2 — there are two different root causes here

### Root cause A: an uncancelled `setTimeout` inside an effect

This is a real leak. Example, `src/components/ui/multi-filter/tagFilter.tsx`:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (!open) {
    setTimeout(() => { onSubMenuOpen(false); }, 100);
  } else {
    onSubMenuOpen(true);
  }
}, [open, onSubMenuOpen]);
```

The timer keeps running after the component unmounts. It then calls a parent callback on a component that is gone. Fix per recipe (A): capture the id and clear it.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (open) { onSubMenuOpen(true); return; }
  const id = setTimeout(() => { onSubMenuOpen(false); }, 100);
  return () => clearTimeout(id);
}, [open, onSubMenuOpen]);
```

`src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationMap.tsx` has the same shape. It calls `setTimeout(() => fitView({...}), ...)` inside an effect. Read the whole effect. Apply the same fix.

### Root cause B: `form.watch(...)` called inside an effect or a helper function

The detector matches `.watch` as a subscription. In react-hook-form, `form.watch("name")` with a string argument reads a value; it does not return an unsubscribe handle. So there is no handle to release. But this is still a real defect, and the correct root-cause fix removes the `.watch` call from the effect.

The react-hook-form documentation says: do not call `watch()` inside an effect or a render-phase helper. Use the `useWatch` hook at the top level of the component. `useWatch` subscribes correctly, re-renders the component when the value changes, and cleans itself up on unmount. `form.watch()` inside an effect reads a value that the effect's dependency array does not track, so the effect can run with a stale value.

So for each of these sites, hoist the reads to `useWatch` at the top level of the component and add the resulting values to the effect dependency array:

```tsx
// before
useEffect(() => {
  const name = form.watch("name");
  const beds = form.watch("numberOfBeds");
  ...
}, [/* name and beds are not tracked */]);

// after
const name = useWatch({ control: form.control, name: "name" });
const beds = useWatch({ control: form.control, name: "numberOfBeds" });
useEffect(() => {
  ...
}, [name, beds]);
```

These files use root cause B:

- `src/components/Tokens/CreateTokenForm.tsx`
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationForm.tsx` (2 sites)
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/observationDefinition/ObservationDefinitionForm.tsx`
- `src/pages/Scheduling/components/CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx` (2 sites)
- `src/pages/Scheduling/components/EditScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx` (2 sites)

Warning: some of these `form.watch` reads sit inside plain helper functions, not inside `useEffect`. Examples: `CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx` around lines 257 and 291, and `ObservationDefinitionForm.tsx` around line 332. Read each one. If the helper runs during render, `useWatch` is still the correct fix. If the helper is an event handler that runs on a user action, `form.getValues("name")` is the correct fix, because a handler must read the current value and must not subscribe. Choose per site, with evidence from the code. Explain each choice in your report.

Caution: `useWatch` re-renders the component whenever the watched field changes. In `CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx` the reads are inside a `useFieldArray` loop with an `index`. Do not put a hook inside a loop or a `.map` callback. That breaks the Rules of Hooks. Extract a child component per row so each row owns its own `useWatch`. This is recipe (B) from the `rules-of-hooks` guidance.

## Step 3 — verify

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass with no new errors.
2. `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose` must report 0 `effect-needs-cleanup` findings. This takes several minutes; use a long timeout and be patient.
3. Confirm you did not add new `rules-of-hooks` or `exhaustive-deps` errors.
4. Test the real behaviour. Run the forms you changed. The bed-name auto-fill in `LocationForm`, the slot calculation in the two schedule sheets, and the category default in `CreateTokenForm` must all still work. Read `docs/local-development.md` and `docs/testing.md`. Run any Playwright test that covers these screens, for example `npx playwright test tests/facility/`.

## Step 4 — pull request

Commit your work and open a pull request with `create_pull_request`.

- Base branch: `develop`.
- Title: `\ud83d\udc1b Cleans up effect timers and replaces form.watch with useWatch`
- Body: explain both root causes in plain language, list the files, and paste the before/after React Doctor output for this rule.

If the change turns out to be too large for one pull request, split root cause A and root cause B into two pull requests. Say so in your report.

## Writing style

Write every comment, commit message and PR description in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use the active voice. Use short sentences. Give one idea per sentence. Do not use jargon.

Use the ask_user tool to ask the user clarifying questions when needed.

**IMPORTANT: Never ask questions via plain text output.** When you need input from the user, use this tool instead of asking in your response text. The tool provides a better UX and ensures the user's answer is captured properly.

Guidelines:
- Prefer multiple choice (provide choices array) over freeform for faster UX
- Do NOT include "Other", "Something else", or similar catch-all choices - the UI automatically adds a freeform input option
- Only use pure freeform (no choices) when the answer truly cannot be predicted
- Ask one question at a time - do not batch multiple questions
- Don't ask the questions in bullet points or numbered lists. Ask each question in a clear sentence or paragraph form.
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first choice and add "(Recommended)" to the label
  Example: choices: ["PostgreSQL (Recommended)", "MySQL", "SQLite"]

Examples:
1. BAD - bundling multiple questions into one and asking the user to confirm or break them apart:
  { "question": "Here's what I'm thinking:\n1. Use PostgreSQL for the database\n2. Add Redis for caching\n3. Use JWT for auth\nDoes this sound good, or would you like to discuss each choice individually?", "choices": ["Sounds good", "Let's discuss individually"] }
  WORKAROUND - ask one focused question per tool call:
  First call:  { "question": "What database should I use?", "choices": ["PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "SQLite"] }
  Second call: { "question": "Should I add Redis for caching?", "choices": ["Yes", "No"] }
  Third call:  { "question": "What auth strategy should I use?", "choices": ["JWT", "Session-based", "OAuth"] }
2. BAD - embedding choices in the question text instead of using the choices field:
  { "question": "What database should I use? (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite)" }
  WORKAROUND - put the options in the choices array:
  { "question": "What database should I use?", "choices": ["PostgreSQL", "MySQL", "SQLite"] }

When to STOP and ask (do not assume):
- Design decisions that significantly affect implementation approach
- Behavioral questions (e.g., "should this be unlimited or capped?")
- Scope ambiguity (e.g., which features to include/exclude)
- Edge cases where multiple reasonable approaches exist

<sql>
**Session database** (database: "session", the default):
The per-session database persists across the session but is isolated from other sessions.

Use SQL for structured operational data such as todo lists, test cases, batch items, and session state.

**Pre-existing tables (ready to use):**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on (for dependency tracking)

**Todo tracking:**
Use descriptive kebab-case IDs (not t1, t2). Write titles in gerund form (e.g. "Creating user auth module"). Include enough detail that the todo can be executed without referring back to the plan:
```sql
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-auth', 'Creating user auth module', 'Implement JWT auth in src/auth/ so login, logout, and token refresh don''t depend on server sessions. Use bcrypt for password hashing.');
```

**Todo status:**
- `pending`: Todo is waiting to be started
- `in_progress`: You are actively working on this todo (set this before starting!)
- `done`: Todo is complete
- `blocked`: Todo cannot proceed (document why in description)

**Dependencies:** Insert into todo_deps when one todo must complete before another:
```sql
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');  -- routes wait for model
```

**Create any tables you need.** The database is yours to use for any purpose:
- Load and query data (CSVs, API responses, file listings)
- Store intermediate results for structured multi-step work
- Query any workflow data that benefits from SQL

Common patterns:

1. **Todo tracking with dependencies:**
```sql
-- todos and todo_deps already exist — do NOT CREATE them, just INSERT:
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts');

-- Find todos with no pending dependencies ("ready" query):
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

2. **Session state (key-value):**
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```
</sql>

<task>
**When to Use Sub-Agents**
* Use a matching specialist when the request specifically calls for that domain expertise.
* For other reviews, audits, and summaries, never delegate parts of a codebase that is small enough to read directly, regardless of how it divides into separate areas; do them yourself. Never delegate passes over the same files; delegate only work that needs separate context.

**When to use explore agent** (not grep/glob):
* Never use explore to split a review, audit, or summary by labeled area when its total scope is small; do it yourself. Reserve explore for independent threads that need substantial separate context.
* For simple lookups — understanding a specific component, finding a symbol, or reading a few known files — do it yourself using grep/glob/view. This is faster and keeps context in your conversation.
* Trace a single continuous chain yourself.
* Do not speculatively launch explore agents in the background "just in case" — they consume resources and rarely finish before you've already found the answer yourself.

**If you do use explore:**
* The explore agent is stateless — provide complete context in each call.
* Batch related questions into one call. Launch independent explorations in parallel.
* Do NOT duplicate its work by calling grep/view on files it already reported.
* Once you have enough information to address the user's request, stop investigating and deliver the result. Don't chase every lead or do redundant follow-up searches.

**When to use custom agents**:
* If both a built-in agent and a custom agent could handle a task, prefer the custom agent as it has specialized knowledge for this environment.

**How to Use Sub-Agents**
* Instruct the sub-agent to do the task itself, not just give advice.
* Once you delegate a scope to an agent, that agent owns it until it completes or fails; do not investigate the same scope yourself.
* If a sub-agent fails repeatedly, do the task yourself.
**Avoiding Unnecessary Sub-Agent Delegation**
* Before delegating, assess whether a direct approach (1-2 tool calls with grep/glob/view) would be faster. Only delegate tasks that genuinely benefit from multi-step autonomous work.
* If a sub-agent completes with 0 useful turns or produces no actionable output, do not re-launch it — fall back to doing the work yourself immediately.

**Background Agents**
* After launching a background agent for work you need before your next step, tell the user you're waiting, then end your response with no tool calls. A completion notification will arrive automatically.
* When that notification arrives, a good default is to call read_agent once with wait: true to retrieve the result. If it still shows running, stop there for this response. Leave same-scope work with the agent while it runs.
* Use read_agent for completed background agents, not to check whether they're done.

**Multi-Turn Conversations**
* Background agents stay alive after responding. Instead of launching a new agent, send follow-up messages with write_agent to refine, correct, or extend the agent's work.
* Prefer write_agent for iterative refinement over launching a new agent — the agent retains its full conversation context.
* Typical workflow: start agent (background) → wait for completion notification → read_agent (get result) → write_agent (send refinement) → wait for notification → read_agent (get updated result).
* Use read_agent with since_turn as an inclusive 0-based start turn.
* Idle agents (status: "idle") are waiting for messages — they're ready to receive write_agent immediately.
</task>

## Local Development Environment

### Backend Setup (care)

Clone the [care backend](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care) alongside this repo and create a Python 3.13 venv with dependencies installed.

**Start backend services:**

```bash
# Ensure PostgreSQL and Redis are running
pg_isready || sudo pg_ctlcluster 16 main start
redis-cli ping || redis-server --daemonize yes

# Start Django backend on port 9000 (from the care backend directory)
cd <care-backend-dir>
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.local DJANGO_READ_DOT_ENV_FILE=true .venv/bin/python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:9000
```

**Database commands:**

```bash
cd <care-backend-dir>
.venv/bin/python manage.py migrate                    # Run migrations
.venv/bin/python manage.py load_fixtures              # Load test data
```

## Build/Lint/Test Commands

- `npm run dev` — Start dev server at http://localhost:4000
- `npm run build` — Production build (takes 2+ minutes, set timeout to 180s+)

- `npm run format` — Prettier formatting

### Playwright E2E Tests

**Prerequisites:** Backend must be running on port 9000, and a production build must exist (`npm run build`).

```bash
npm run playwright:install                              # Install browsers (first time)
npm run build                                           # Build app (tests run against production build)
npm run playwright:test                                 # Run all tests
npm run playwright:test -- tests/auth/login.spec.ts     # Run a single test file
npm run playwright:test -- -g "test name"               # Run tests matching a pattern
npm run playwright:test -- --workers=4                   # Run with 4 parallel workers
npm run playwright:test -- --shard=1/3                   # Run shard 1 of 3
npm run playwright:test:ui                              # Interactive Playwright UI mode
```

**Running tests efficiently:**

- Use `--workers=4` for parallel execution (CI runs setup with 1 worker, then chromium with 4 workers)
- Use `--shard=N/TOTAL` to split across multiple processes
- Run specific test directories to iterate faster: `npx playwright test tests/auth/`
- The `setup` project runs first to authenticate test users and save storage state

**Database management for re-runs:**

Tests create data (patients, roles, locations, etc.) that can cause conflicts on re-run. Use the DB snapshot system:

```bash
# Set CARE_BACKEND_DIR to your care backend checkout (required for db-reset)
export CARE_BACKEND_DIR=/path/to/care

npm run playwright:db-reset      # First time: migrate + fixtures + snapshot (~30s)
npm run playwright:db-restore    # Before re-runs: restore clean state (~2s)
npm run playwright:db-snapshot   # Save current state as new baseline
npm run playwright:db-status     # Check snapshot info
```

The `globalSetup` automatically restores the DB snapshot before each local test run (skipped on CI). To set up for the first time:

```bash
npm run playwright:db-reset      # Creates snapshot with fixtures
npm run playwright:test           # Tests run against clean DB, auto-restores on next run
```

**Test structure:**

- `tests/setup/` — Authentication & fixture setup (runs before tests)
- `tests/auth/` — Login, session, homepage tests
- `tests/facility/` — Facility management, settings, patients, encounters
- `tests/admin/` — Admin panel tests
- `tests/organization/` — Organization management
- `tests/helper/` — Shared test utilities
- `tests/support/` — ID management (facility, patient, encounter IDs)

**Writing new tests:**

- Use `faker` for data generation — avoid hardcoded names/slugs that collide on re-run
- Use `Date.now()` or `faker.string.alphanumeric()` for unique identifiers
- Don't rely on cleanup — the DB snapshot system handles state reset
- Use `getFacilityId()`, `getPatientId()`, `getEncounterId()` from `tests/support/` for fixture IDs

## Code Style Guidelines

- **TypeScript**: Strict mode, ES2022 target, path aliases (`@/*` → `src/*`, `@careConfig` → `care.config.ts`)
- **Formatting**: Double quotes, 2-space indent, semicolons required
- **Imports**: Order by 3rd-party → library → CAREUI → UI → components → hooks → utils → relative. Prettier plugin auto-sorts on format.
- **Types**: Use `interface` for objects, avoid `any`, prefer maps over enums
- **Naming**: PascalCase for component files (`AuthWizard.tsx`), camelCase for hooks/utils (`useAuth.ts`), kebab-case for directories
- **Components**: Functional components only, named exports preferred, one component per file
- **i18n**: All user-facing strings must use i18next. English translations go in `public/locale/en.json`. Non-English managed via Crowdin — do not edit directly.

## Architecture

### Routing (Raviger)

Routes defined in `src/Routers/routes/` (e.g., `FacilityRoutes.tsx`, `PatientRoutes.tsx`). Combined in `src/Routers/AppRouter.tsx`. Three routers: `PublicRouter`, `PatientRouter`, `AppRouter` — selected by auth state. Plugin routes injected via `usePluginRoutes()`.

```typescript
const FacilityRoutes: AppRoutes = {
  "/facility/:facilityId/overview": ({ facilityId }) => <FacilityOverview facilityId={facilityId} />,
};
```

Use `navigate()` from raviger for programmatic navigation.

### API Layer (TanStack Query + custom wrappers)

API routes defined in `src/types/{domain}/{domain}Api.ts` using typed route objects:

```typescript
export default {
  list: {
    path: "/api/v1/users/",
    method: HttpMethod.GET,
    TRes: Type<PaginatedResponse<UserReadMinimal>>(),
  },
} as const;
```

Queries use `query()` wrapper from `src/Utils/request/query.ts`:

```typescript
const { data } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ["users"],
  queryFn: query(userApi.list),
});
// With path/query params:
queryFn: query(userApi.get, {
  pathParams: { username },
  queryParams: { search },
});
```

Mutations use `mutate()` wrapper from `src/Utils/request/mutate.ts`:

```typescript
const { mutate } = useMutation({
  mutationFn: mutate(userApi.create),
});
```

Also available: `query.debounced()` and `query.paginated()` for specialized use cases.

Errors handled globally — session expiry redirects to `/session-expired`, 400/406 show toast notifications. Use `silent: true` to suppress.

### State Management

- **TanStack Query** — Server state (API data caching, refetching)
- **Jotai atoms** (`src/atoms/`) — Lightweight client state (user, nav, filters)
- **React Context** (`src/context/`) — Permissions (`PermissionContext`), keyboard shortcuts

### UI Components

Built on **shadcn/ui** + **Radix UI primitives** + **Tailwind CSS v4** (shadcn/ui pattern):

- `src/components/ui/` — Base UI primitives (Button, Dialog, Form, Select, etc.). Do not modify these directly.
- `src/CAREUI/` — Custom healthcare icon library, use `lucide-react` unless you are explicitly asked to use CAREUI icons.
- Forms use `react-hook-form` + `zod` validation with the custom `<Form>` component

### Plugin System (Module Federation)

Micro-frontend architecture via `@originjs/vite-plugin-federation`. Plugins configured via `REACT_ENABLED_APPS` env var. Plugin manifests define routes, components, tabs, and devices they provide. Key files: `src/PluginEngine.tsx`, `src/pluginTypes.ts`.

### Auth Flow

JWT tokens in localStorage. `AuthUserProvider` handles login/logout, token refresh (every 5 minutes), 2FA, and cross-tab session sync. Patient login uses separate OTP-based flow via `PatientRouter`.

### Key Directories

- `src/components/` — Feature-organized components (Auth, Facility, Patient, Encounter, Medicine, etc.)
- `src/pages/` — Page components by feature (Admin, Appointments, Facility, Organization, Patient)
- `src/types/` — Domain type definitions with corresponding `*Api.ts` route files
- `src/Utils/request/` — API request infrastructure (query, mutate, error handling)
- `src/hooks/` — Custom React hooks (auth, file management, plugins, etc.)
- `src/Providers/` — Auth, history, patient user providers
- `src/Routers/` — App routing and route definitions

### Configuration

`care.config.ts` centralizes runtime config (API URLs, feature flags, locale settings, plugin config). Environment variables prefixed with `REACT_`.

## Autonomous AI Workflow

When working autonomously on this codebase, follow this sequence:

1. **Before coding:** Read relevant source files and understand existing patterns
2. **After changes:** Run `npm run lint-fix` and `npm run format` on changed files (pre-commit hooks also run these automatically)
3. **Verify:** Run relevant Playwright tests against the local backend to validate changes
4. **For API changes:** Check corresponding backend endpoint in the care backend repo and update both repos if needed
5. **For new features:** Add Playwright tests in `tests/` following `tests/PLAYWRIGHT_GUIDE.md`
6. **For i18n:** Add English strings to `public/locale/en.json`
7. **For writing tests:** Read `tests/PLAYWRIGHT_GUIDE.md` — it contains complete patterns for all form interactions, selectors, assertions, and helpers

### Quick verification cycle

```bash
# 1. Lint & format (or rely on pre-commit hooks)
npm run lint-fix && npm run format

# 2. Type check
npx tsc --noEmit

# 3. Run related tests (requires backend + build)
npx playwright test tests/path/to/related/
```

Rule: react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup
Severity: error
Category: Bugs
Count: 11

`watch` creates a subscription in useEffect without guaranteed cleanup. Return a cleanup function that owns every allocation so it does not leak after unmount.

`setTimeout` creates a timer in useEffect without guaranteed cleanup. Return a cleanup function that owns every allocation so it does not leak after unmount.

`watch` creates a subscription in a function that outlives the render, with no cleanup path. Store the handle and release it, or move this into a useEffect that returns cleanup, so it does not leak after unmount.

Suggestion: Return a cleanup function that stops the subscription or timer: `return () => target.removeEventListener(name, handler)` for listeners, `return () => clearInterval(id)` or `clearTimeout(id)` for timers, `return () => observer.disconnect()` for observers, `return () => socket.close()` for connections, or `return unsubscribe` if the subscribe call already gave you one.

#!/bin/bash
# Playwright database management for local development
# Handles snapshot/restore of the care database for repeatable test runs
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/playwright-db.sh snapshot   — Save current DB state as test baseline
#   ./scripts/playwright-db.sh restore    — Restore DB to the saved snapshot
#   ./scripts/playwright-db.sh reset      — Drop, recreate, migrate, and load fixtures
#   ./scripts/playwright-db.sh status     — Show snapshot info

set -e

SNAPSHOT_FILE="${PLAYWRIGHT_DB_SNAPSHOT:-/tmp/care_playwright_snapshot.dump}"
DB_NAME="${POSTGRES_DB:-care}"
DB_USER="${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}"
DB_HOST="${POSTGRES_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
DB_PORT="${POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}"

export PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-postgres}"

pg_cmd() {
  "$@" -h "$DB_HOST" -p "$DB_PORT" -U "$DB_USER"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  snapshot)
    echo "Taking DB snapshot → $SNAPSHOT_FILE"
    pg_cmd pg_dump -Fc "$DB_NAME" -f "$SNAPSHOT_FILE"
    echo "Snapshot saved ($(du -h "$SNAPSHOT_FILE" | cut -f1))"
    ;;

  restore)
    if [ ! -f "$SNAPSHOT_FILE" ]; then
      echo "No snapshot found at $SNAPSHOT_FILE"
      echo "Run './scripts/playwright-db.sh snapshot' first, or './scripts/playwright-db.sh reset' to create a fresh one."
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "Restoring DB from snapshot..."
    # Terminate existing connections
    pg_cmd psql -d postgres -c "SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = '$DB_NAME' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid();" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true

data.summaryContent:
<overview>
A cross-session message asked me to fix exactly one React Doctor rule in the `ohcnetwork/care_fe` repository — `react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup` (severity error, category Bugs, P1) — and then open a pull request against `develop`. The finding had 12 reported occurrences, one of which was in a file that does not exist on `develop`.

The work has two distinct root causes: (A) uncancelled `setTimeout` calls inside `useEffect`, and (B) `form.watch(...)` calls from react-hook-form used inside effects or helper functions. All code fixes are complete and verified (tsc clean, ESLint 0 errors, React Doctor 11 → 0 for this rule, 54 targeted Playwright tests pass). The remaining work is a final manual behaviour check of `CreateTokenForm`, cleanup of temporary test files, commit, and PR creation.

All output (comments, commit message, PR body, chat replies) must be in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: active voice, short sentences, one idea per sentence, no jargon.
</overview>

<history>
1. The cross-session message asked me to fix `react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup` and open a PR.
   - Renamed the branch to `rithviknishad/effect-needs-cleanup` using the `rename_branch` tool.
   - Fetched and read the canonical recipe from `https://react.doctor/docs/rules/react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup.md` into `/tmp/rd-cleanup.md`.

2. Confirmed the reported missing file.
   - `find src -name "useMedicationBill*"` returned nothing. `src/pages/Facility/services/pharmacy/hooks/useMedicationBill.ts` does **not** exist. Only `useUpdateDispenseOrderStatus.ts` is in that folder. Skipped it, as instructed.

3. Established the React Doctor baseline.
   - Ran `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose > /tmp/rd-before.txt`.
   - Baseline: **11** `effect-needs-cleanup` findings (not 12). Line numbers matched the given list exactly.
   - Baseline overall: score 43, errors 21, warnings 1313.
   - Found the per-rule detail file in the temp diagnostics dir, which revealed a **third** detector message variant: "`watch` creates a subscription in a function that outlives the render, with no cleanup path." This explained why plain helper functions (not just effects) were flagged.

4. Read every flagged site and classified each one.
   - Confirmed which helpers run during render versus which run only from event handlers, by grepping for call sites.

5. Applied the fixes across 7 files.

6. Verified.
   - `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`: only one error, `Cannot find module '@/supportedBrowsers'`, proven pre-existing by stashing and re-running.
   - Hit and fixed a real type error: `Control<TIn, unknown, TOut>` vs `Control<T>`.
   - `npx prettier --write` and `npx eslint` on changed files: warnings dropped 15 → 9, errors 0.
   - Ran React Doctor again: `effect-needs-cleanup` **11 → 0**. Score 43 → 46, errors 21 → 10, warnings 1313 → 1306. A full per-rule diff showed **no rule got worse**; `exhaustive-deps` improved 72 → 66 and `no-adjust-state-on-prop-change` 97 → 96.

7. Ran Playwright E2E tests.
   - Created `.env.local` with `REACT_CARE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000` (the local backend was already running on port 9000; all fixture users log in with status 200).
   - Deliberately did **not** run `playwright:db-reset`, because it drops and recreates the developer's database. No snapshot existed, so `globalSetup` just logged a warning and continued.
   - `npm run build` then `npx playwright test --project=setup --workers=1`: 8 passed.
   - First targeted run with `--workers=4`: 41 passed, 4 failed — all in `observationDefinition.spec.ts`.
   - Investigated the failures honestly: stashed changes, rebuilt, ran the baseline → 19/19 passed. Restored changes, rebuilt, re-ran → 2 failed, but a **different** subset. Re-ran again → 1 failed, again a different subset. Ran with `--workers=1` → 19/19 passed.
   - Proved the flakiness is pre-existing: stashed, rebuilt, ran the baseline 3 times with `--workers=4` → run 1 failed 1 test, runs 2 and 3 passed. So the failures are a pre-existing parallel-worker race on the shared database, not caused by my change.
   - Final targeted run with changes and `--workers=1` across locations, userScheduleCreation, observationDefinition, tokenCategory, tags and queues: **54 passed**.

8. Started manual verification of `CreateTokenForm`, which has no E2E coverage.
   - Discovered `CreateTokenForm` is rendered only from `src/pages/Patient/PatientHome.tsx`, behind the flag `careConfig.enableTokenGenerationInPatientHome`, which defaults to `false`.
   - Added `REACT_ENABLE_TOKEN_GENERATION_IN_PATIENT_HOME=true` to `.env.local` and rebuilt successfully.
   - Compaction occurred at this point, before the manual check ran.
</history>

<work_done>
Files modified (7, all still uncommitted working-tree changes on branch `rithviknishad/effect-needs-cleanup`):

**Root cause A — uncancelled timers**

- `src/components/ui/multi-filter/tagFilter.tsx` (~line 423, in `GroupSubmenu`): inverted the branch so the open case returns early, captured the timer id in `timeoutId`, and returned `() => clearTimeout(timeoutId)`.
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationMap.tsx` (~lines 417 and 435, in `LocationMapContent`): captured both `fitView` timer ids as `fitViewTimeoutId` and returned `() => clearTimeout(fitViewTimeoutId)` from inside each `if` block.

**Root cause B — `form.watch` misuse**

- `src/components/Tokens/CreateTokenForm.tsx` (~line 114): the effect previously did `form.setValue("categoryId", "")` and then guarded on `!form.watch("categoryId")`, which is always true after that `setValue`. Removed the dead read. The effect now computes `options` once and calls `setValue` once, with `?? ""` as the final fallback and optional chaining on `options?.[0]?.id` (this also removes a latent crash when `options` is empty).
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationForm.tsx`: hoisted 5 reads (`form`, `enableBulkCreation`, `numberOfBeds`, `name`, `customizeNames`) to `useWatch` at the top level. Wrapped `resetToDefaultNames` in `useCallback`. Replaced the dependency array, which previously contained live `form.watch(...)` calls, with the `useWatch` values plus `form`, `replaceBedFields` and `resetToDefaultNames`. Imports changed to `useCallback` and `useWatch`.
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/observationDefinition/ObservationDefinitionForm.tsx` (~line 332): `handleClearObservationInterpretation` runs only from an `AlertDialogAction` `onClick`, so `form.watch("component")` became `form.getValues("component")`.
- `src/pages/Scheduling/components/CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx`: hoisted the whole zod schema to a module-scope factory `buildTemplateFormSchema(t: TFunction)`; added `type TemplateFormSchema` and `type TemplateFormControl`. Extracted the render helper `timeAllocationCallout(index)` into a new module-scope component `TimeAllocationCallout({ control, index })` that uses 4 `useWatch` calls. Changed the JSX call site to `<TimeAllocationCallout control={form.control} index={index} />`. Converted `updateSlotDuration(index)` to `form.getValues(...)`. Imports changed to add `TFunction` from `i18next` and `Control`, `useWatch` from `react-hook-form`.
- `src/pages/Scheduling/components/EditScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx` (in `NewAvailabilityCard`, which starts at line 539): hoisted `startTime`, `endTime`, `slotSizeInMinutes`, `tokensPerSlot` to `useWatch` right after `useForm` and before the early `if (!isExpanded) return` — so the Rules of Hooks stay satisfied. `timeAllocationCallout()` now reads those variables. `updateSlotDuration()` converted to `form.getValues(...)`. Import changed to `useForm, useWatch`.

Untracked local files created (must be handled before commit):
- `.env.local` — contains `REACT_CARE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000` and `REACT_ENABLE_TOKEN_GENERATION_IN_PATIENT_HOME=true`. It is in `.gitignore` (line 18), so it will not be committed. It should be reverted to just the API URL line, or removed, at the end.
- `tests/tmp-token-check.spec.ts` — a temporary probe spec. **This is tracked-path scratch and must be deleted before commit.**

Verification completed:
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — no new errors (one pre-existing `@/supportedBrowsers` error confirmed on the clean tree).
- [x] Prettier + ESLint — 0 errors; warnings for changed files dropped 15 → 9.
- [x] React Doctor — `effect-needs-cleanup` 11 → 0; no other rule regressed; no new `rules-of-hooks` (only the pre-existing `src/pages/Facility/utils/useCurrentFacility.tsx:39`); `exhaustive-deps` improved.
- [x] Playwright — 54 targeted tests pass with `--workers=1`, including `locationCreation.spec.ts` "preserves a customized bed name when the bed count changes" (directly covers the `LocationForm` fix) and `userScheduleCreation.spec.ts` "should create and verify a weekday schedule template" (covers `CreateScheduleTemplateSheet`).
- [ ] Manual check of `CreateTokenForm` default-category behaviour — build with the flag on succeeded, but the check itself did not run.
- [ ] Delete the temp spec, restore `.env.local`, commit, open the PR.

Most recent action: `npm run build` finished with exit 0 after adding `REACT_ENABLE_TOKEN_GENERATION_IN_PATIENT_HOME=true` to `.env.local`.
</work_done>

<technical_details>
- The detector fires on three shapes, not two. The third message — "`watch` creates a subscription in a function that outlives the render, with no cleanup path" — explains why plain helper functions were flagged, not only `useEffect` bodies. The per-rule text files inside the temp diagnostics directory carry these messages; the console output does not.
- Decision rule applied at each `form.watch` site: if the helper runs during render, use `useWatch`; if it runs only from a user event, use `form.getValues`. Evidence came from grepping call sites.
  - `CreateTokenForm` effect → neither; the read was provably dead code, so removing it is the true root-cause fix. Using `useWatch` there would have created a loop, because the effect itself writes `categoryId`.
  - `LocationForm.resetToDefaultNames` → called from both an effect and an `onClick`, so `useWatch` values plus `useCallback` serve both.
  - `ObservationDefinitionForm.handleClearObservationInterpretation` → `onClick` only → `getValues`.
  - `CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.timeAllocationCallout` → render phase inside a `.map` over `useFieldArray` → child component with `useWatch` (a hook cannot go in a loop).
  - `CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.updateSlotDuration` → `onChange`/`onCheckedChange` only → `getValues`.
  - `EditScheduleTemplateSheet.timeAllocationCallout` → render phase but **no loop** → hoist `useWatch` to the component top level, no child component needed.
  - `EditScheduleTemplateSheet.updateSlotDuration` → event handlers only → `getValues`.
- Typing gotcha: `useForm` with `zodResolver` produces `Control<TInput, unknown, TOutput>`, not `Control<T>`. Using `Control<z.infer<...>>` fails with a confusing "Two different types with this name exist" error. The fix was `Control<z.input<S>, unknown, z.output<S>>`. This forced the schema to move to a module-scope factory so the type could be named outside the component.
- `npx tsc` does not work in this repo; it prints "This is not the tsc command you are looking for". Use `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`.
- The build output directory is `build/`, not `dist/`.
- `observationDefinition.spec.ts` is **flaky under `--workers=4`** on a shared local database. The failing subset changes on every run, and the unmodified baseline also fails. 🐛 Cleans up effect timers and replaces form.watch with useWatch

This commit corrects 11 findings of the React Doctor rule
`react-doctor/effect-needs-cleanup`. The findings have two causes.

Cause A: an effect starts a timer but does not stop it.
The timer runs after React removes the component. It then calls a
callback on a component that is gone. The fix keeps the timer id and
clears the timer in the cleanup function.

Files:
- src/components/ui/multi-filter/tagFilter.tsx
- src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationMap.tsx

Cause B: the code calls `form.watch(...)` in an effect or in a helper
function. A read with `form.watch` does not give a handle to release.
The effect also does not track the value that it reads. So the effect
can use an old value. The fix depends on when the code runs:
- Code that runs during render now uses the `useWatch` hook at the top
  level of a component. The values go into the dependency array.
- Code that runs only after a user action now uses `form.getValues`.
  A handler must read the current value. A handler must not subscribe.

Files:
- src/components/Tokens/CreateTokenForm.tsx
- src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationForm.tsx
- src/pages/Facility/settings/observationDefinition/ObservationDefinitionForm.tsx
- src/pages/Scheduling/components/CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx
- src/pages/Scheduling/components/EditScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx

In CreateScheduleTemplateSheet.tsx the reads sit in a loop over a field
array. A hook must not go in a loop. So a new child component
`TimeAllocationCallout` holds the `useWatch` calls. Each row owns its
own subscription.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
EOF
